heroIntro: Selling inherited real estate in Bangladesh and transferring the sale proceeds to the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia is one of the most critical financial and legal challenges facing Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs). Under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and Bangladesh Bank Foreign Exchange Guidelines, outward foreign currency remittances require strict regulatory compliance, source of funds verification, National Board of Revenue (NBR) tax clearance, and central bank permission. Without proper legal structuring, expatriates risk severe capital lock-in or penalties under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012.

quickAnswer.heading: Repatriating Property Sale Funds: The 6-Step Rule
points: Establish indisputable legal title, Warishan Certificate, and e-Namjari mutation in your name prior to sale.
Execute the sale deed through an appointed Attorney or in person at the local Sub-Registry Office.
Receive 100% of the sale consideration via account-payee cheque, bank draft, or RTGS into an official bank account in Bangladesh.
Deduct and pay statutory Source Tax (Section 125 Income Tax Act 2023) and Capital Gains Tax to the NBR.
Obtain a formal Tax Clearance Certificate (কর ছাড়পত্র) from the competent Taxes Circle of NBR.
Apply through an Authorized Dealer (AD) Bank to Bangladesh Bank for outward remittance approval under Form TM.

sections.h2: The Legal Framework: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947
sections.content:
Cross-border transfer of capital and asset sale proceeds is regulated by Section 4 and 5 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947, supplemented by the Guidelines for Foreign Exchange Transactions (GFET, Vol-1 & Vol-2) issued by Bangladesh Bank.

Bangladeshi foreign exchange policy strictly distinguishes between current account transactions (such as trade payments and university tuition) and capital account transactions (such as remitting real estate liquidation proceeds). Because Bangladesh maintains capital account convertibility restrictions, an expatriate cannot simply convert millions of Taka into US Dollars or British Pounds at a commercial bank counter without formal Central Bank sanction.

sections.h2: Prerequisite: Clean Title, Inheritance Proof & Mutation
sections.content:
Before advertising or accepting advance token money for property in Dhaka, Sylhet, or Chittagong, overseas owners must ensure their ownership papers are entirely unassailable:

  • Succession / Warishan Certificate: Issued by the Mayor or Union Parishad Chairman confirming legal heirs of the deceased parent.
  • Up-to-Date e-Namjari (ই-নামজারি ও ডিহি জমা খারিজ): The property must be recorded in the Land Reforms Board database in the names of the living heirs, not the deceased parent.
  • Up-to-Date Land Development Tax (ভূমি উন্নয়ন কর - দাখিলা): All land holding taxes must be paid online via ldtax.gov.bd up to the current fiscal year.
  • Non-Encumbrance Certificate (NEC): Proving the property is free from bank mortgage or court attachment.

sections.h2: Executing the Sale Deed & Receiving Sale Proceeds Safely
sections.content:
When disposing of land or apartments, expatriates must avoid accepting cash payments. All consideration must be transacted through banking channels:

  1. Account-Payee Cheque or Pay Order: Must be drawn directly from the purchaser's verified bank account into the seller's resident or non-resident bank account in Bangladesh.
  2. Real-Time Gross Settlement (RTGS): For high-value transactions, direct electronic bank transfer ensures instantaneous audit traceability.
  3. Stated Deed Value vs Actual Market Value: Under-reporting deed value to evade registration fees is illegal under Bangladeshi law and severely diminishes the amount of money you can legally remit overseas, because Bangladesh Bank only permits remittance equal to the net declared value on the registered deed minus taxes.

sections.h2: Taxation on Property Sales: Source Tax & Capital Gains Tax (2026)
sections.content:
Under the Income Tax Act, 2023 (আয়কর আইন, ২০২৩), real estate transfers are subject to specific fiscal deductions:

  • Advance Tax at Source (Section 125): Deducted at the Sub-Registry office at the time of deed registration. The rate varies from 2% to 8% depending on the location of the land (e.g., higher within RAJUK, CDA, or commercial zones).
  • Capital Gains Tax (Section 89): Levied on the net profit realized between the acquisition cost and the final sale consideration. Expatriates must file an assessment statement with the relevant NBR Deputy Commissioner of Taxes (DCT).
  • Obtaining Tax Clearance (কর প্রত্যয়নপত্র): The NBR issues an official certificate confirming that all tax obligations on the sale proceeds have been satisfied. This certificate is mandatory for Bangladesh Bank remittance processing.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Bangladesh Bank Outward Remittance Approval
sections.content:
The process of obtaining outward remittance approval involves an Authorized Dealer (AD) commercial bank (e.g., Standard Chartered, HSBC, BRAC Bank, City Bank):

  1. The expatriate or their legal counsel submits an outward remittance application under Form TM (Transfer of Money) to the Foreign Exchange Department of the AD Bank.
  2. The AD Bank reviews the title chain, registered sale deed, tax clearance certificate, proof of inheritance, and foreign residency documents.
  3. The AD Bank forwards the comprehensive file to the Foreign Exchange Policy Department (FEPD) of Bangladesh Bank, Motijheel, Dhaka.
  4. Upon scrutiny, Bangladesh Bank issues a formal permission letter authorizing the AD bank to remit the foreign currency equivalent to the seller's overseas bank account in New York, London, Toronto, etc.

sections.h2: Using NITA / NRTA Bank Accounts for Foreign Remittance
sections.content:
NRBs can hold specialized bank accounts in Bangladesh:

  • Non-Resident Investor's Taka Account (NITA): Primarily intended for foreign investors and NRBs trading in securities. Inflow of foreign currency is freely convertible, and disinvestment proceeds can be repatriated without prior Bangladesh Bank approval.
  • Non-Resident Foreign Currency Deposit (NFCD) / Resident Foreign Currency Deposit (RFCD): Excellent for parking US Dollars, GBP, or Euros with attractive tax-free interest yields.
  • Private Remittance Quota: Under recent Bangladesh Bank circulars, genuine inheritance and real estate liquidation proceeds can be remitted up to authorized thresholds per fiscal year under controlled approval routes.

sections.h2: Dangers of Informal Remittance (Hundi) & Anti-Money Laundering Risks
sections.content:
Some expats consider using informal networks (Hundi / Hawala) due to banking paperwork. This carries catastrophic legal risks:

Transferring property sale proceeds through underground channels violates Section 4 of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012, carrying prison sentences up to 12 years and forfeiture of the entire funds. Furthermore, tax authorities in the US (IRS FATCA compliance), UK (HMRC Unexplained Wealth Orders), and Canada (CRA FINTRAC reporting) will flag large untraceable wire transfers entering domestic accounts without verified bank-to-bank SWIFT documentation.

sections.h2: Checklist of Mandatory Documents for Bangladesh Bank Approval
sections.content:
Prepare this documentation package with your advocate:

  • Original certified copy of the Registered Sale Deed (সাফ কবলা দলিল).
  • Chain of title deeds spanning minimum 25 years (CS, SA, RS, BS records).
  • Original Succession / Warishan Certificate and family lineage tree.
  • NBR Tax Clearance Certificate and Treasury Chalan receipts.
  • Form TM duly completed and signed by the applicant or authorized attorney.
  • Proof of overseas residence (US Green Card/Passport, UK Indefinite Leave/Passport, Canadian PR/Passport).
  • Original bank statement showing deposit of sale proceeds into the seller's account.

faqs.question: Can I transfer the full amount from selling my house in Bangladesh to my US or UK bank account?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided you obtain formal outward remittance approval from Bangladesh Bank through an Authorized Dealer commercial bank, supported by NBR tax clearance and verified registered sale deeds.

faqs.question: How much tax do I have to pay when selling land in Bangladesh as an expat?
faqs.answer: You must pay advance source tax (typically 2% to 8% depending on location) at the time of deed registration, plus applicable capital gains tax assessed under the Income Tax Act 2023.

faqs.question: How long does Bangladesh Bank approval take for outward remittance?
faqs.answer: A well-prepared file submitted through an Authorized Dealer bank typically takes between 4 to 8 weeks for central bank scrutiny and final clearance.

faqs.question: Will the US IRS or UK HMRC tax my land sale proceeds from Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: The US and UK tax residents on worldwide income. However, bilateral Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) usually allow you to claim Foreign Tax Credits (FTC) for taxes already paid to the Bangladesh government.

faqs.question: Can my appointed attorney wire the money to my foreign bank account directly?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the Power of Attorney specifically empowers the attorney to handle banking transactions, apply for Bangladesh Bank permission, and sign Form TM on your behalf.
